Here, we observe a scale-free boundary mode exhibiting anomalous polynomial decay, highlighted by strictly linear spatial envelopes, driven by topological multicriticality in acoustic metamaterials. We establish a universal geometric bulk-boundary correspondence rooted in singularity theory by mapping n-th order topological multicriticality onto Arnold An catastrophe. We prove that defectiveness in the spatial transfer matrix enforces a (n-1)-th power spatial decay of boundary modes. At a topological tri-critical point, the singularity of winding function manifests as an A2 fold catastrophe. This dictates a strictly linear spatial decay, marking a sharp departure from the conventional exponential scaling paradigm. Using acoustic metamaterial platforms tuned to a tricritical point, we experimentally demonstrate this linear decay envelope in 1D, and further generalize it to two-dimensional systems to realize scale-free corner modes with simultaneous linear decay along orthogonal directions. While existing critical topology frameworks rely on entanglement spectra to diagnose mode existence in gapless regimes, our work bridges catastrophe theory with topological matter at multicriticalities, advancing the field from abstract mode identification to deterministic real-space wavefunction engineering.

papers.title: Multistable nematic liquid crystal pores as reconfigurable optical vortex metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Nematic liquid crystals confined in cylindrical pores adopt multiple stable director topologies --- radial, escaped, and arches --- each imprinting a distinct optical signature on transmitted circularly polarized light, with topological charge set by the projected director winding number, $\ell = 2m$. Using Landau--de Gennes and Jones-calculus modeling validated against micron-scale experiments, we show that this mechanism persists as the pore diameter shrinks toward the optical wavelength. However, full-wave Maxwell simulations of periodic sub-wavelength pore arrays reveal that the resulting vortex is a near-field phenomenon only: each topology imprints a distinguishable phase-singular signature --- differing in core multiplicity, core width, and ring amplitude --- directly below the pore array, but this signature does not survive propagation into the far field, where diffraction and inter-pore interference erase it within about one wavelength. Landau--de Gennes simulations further demonstrate that an applied electric field switches the pore between topologies, and hence between their near-field optical signatures. Because each topology is locally stable, sub-wavelength NLC pore arrays constitute an electrically reconfigurable, non-volatile platform for topology-encoded near-field optical readout, with potential application to optical labeling and anti-counterfeiting.

papers.title: Dynamic Behaviors of Materials Under Angle-Resolved Experiments: A Matrix Framework for Nonlinear Physics
papers.abstract: Matter and external stimuli interact dynamically almost everywhere in nature. Under an applied field, a material seldom stays in the state in which it was characterized, and its properties change with time. Angle-resolved experiments are the standard way to resolve direction-dependent properties, however, current theoretical tools for data analysis are built for static states, leaving dynamic behaviors largely neglected. Here, we develop a generalized ``input-coefficient-output'' (ICO) approach that constructs spatial operation matrices and symmetry-reduced coefficient matrices across diverse physical systems, as we verify for nonlinear optics, elasticity, electrostriction and magnetostriction, and a Python program is released for convenient application. Using angle-resolved polarized second-harmonic generation (SHG) as an example, we focus on the dynamic modeling of material properties under angle-dependent stimuli, construct dynamic matrix equations that capture the time-dependent evolution of material responses, and propose three dynamic models and a point-to-point data fitting method. For the SHG experiments performed on $T_d-$WTe$_2$, the discrete dynamic model captures the asymmetric characteristics of the measured polar pattern with a significantly improved coefficient of determination ($R^2$ increasing from 0.567 to 0.773), whereas conventional static models are constrained to a symmetric curve. The evolution operator extracted from the dynamic model connects the macroscopic measurement to microscopic intermediate states during their interaction with stimuli. This work provides a practical matrix framework for dynamic modeling of material properties, paving the way for exploring complex nonlinear physics under realistic experimental conditions.

papers.title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
papers.abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches $h/4e^2$, consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

papers.title: Magnetotransport experiments on side-contacted topological insulator three-terminal Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions have recently attracted substantial attention. The ability to study Andreev bound states in a multi-phase parameter space opens up exciting avenues for generating topologically non-trivial phases in superconducting devices. A particularly interesting case is the trijunction based on a topological insulator (TI), which is predicted to host Majorana zero modes for suitable phase configurations (Fu and Kane, PRL 2008). Here we turn to the platform of the side-contacted TI trijunction and present experimental evidence for a multiterminal Josephson effect. We study the transport properties and find typical features of a two-dimensional critical current contour (CCC) as well as bias regimes in which only a single junction remains dissipationless. We pay particular attention to these features and study the effects of magnetic fields on single junctions within the trijunction, where, depending on the field direction, the supercurrents show Fraunhofer patterns, SQUID oscillations, or a monotonic decay. We find good agreement with semiclassical simulations for a single TI junction that take into account the top and bottom surface states. We observe pronounced non-convex shape deformations of the CCC under perpendicular magnetic fields that reflect the flux buildup in the loop formed by our trijunctions and provide a simple model sufficient to explain the observed effect. Our results provide the foundations for future studies of Majorana zero modes on this platform.

papers.title: Curvature-stabilized three-dimensional spiral states and local-field nucleation of skyrmions on spherical caps
papers.abstract: The combination of polystyrene particles and multilayers with chiral interfacial interactions offers an interesting platform to study the interplay between topology, chirality, and curvature. Here, we investigate Pt/Co/Ta multilayers sputtered onto self-assembled polystyrene particles with a diameter of 919 nm, which show a magnetic reversal distinctly different from that of planar films. Using non-invasive scanning transmission X-ray microscopy and in-vacuum magnetic force microscopy (MFM) with low-moment tips, we observe maze domains in the planar films, whereas the curvilinear films host three-dimensional spiraling stripe states. Repeated scanning with a conventional higher-moment MFM tip ruptures these spirals into metastable skyrmions at the top of the particles. Micromagnetic simulations of spherical caps reveal that increasing curvature renders a single spiral stripe energetically favorable over an isolated skyrmion, and that this stabilization is predominantly of magnetostatic origin. Our results identify the spiral states as intrinsic to the curvilinear geometry and the skyrmions as metastable states nucleated by local magnetic fields, underlining the value of non-invasive imaging to distinguish intrinsic curvature effects from probe-induced magnetic textures.

papers.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
papers.abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

papers.title: Unlimited-Range Absolute Distance Interferometry Outdoors via Tunable Synthetic and Pseudo-Supersynthetic Wavelengths: The TeleYAG-II Interferometer
papers.abstract: Absolute distance interferometry requires an unlimited non-ambiguity range to be truly absolute. Tunable synthetic wavelength interferometry allows for the construction of pseudo-supersynthetic wavelengths using a limited number of optical sources and a standard interferometer setup. This approach facilitates the creation of a series of consecutively deployable synthetic wavelengths, ultimately combining macroscopic unambiguity with microscopic interferometric accuracy. We have implemented and demonstrated this concept in the TeleYAG-II interferometer, designed as an SI-traceable standard for the calibration of geodetic baselines. The system employs two Nd:YAG lasers as optical sources, with their frequency difference controlled by a versatile optical phase-locked loop. Specifically engineered for robustness in field conditions, the heterodyne interferometer was validated through an outdoor measurement campaign. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the method, achieving an expanded measurement uncertainty of 0.13 mm over a distance of 224 m without the need for auxiliary length measurements.

papers.title: Measuring the Value of Communication in Multi-Agent Tracking Under Finite-Rate Belief Sharing
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the value of communica- tion (VoC) in cooperative multi-agent tracking under rate- constrained information exchange. Although prior work has studied distributed tracking, quantized communication, and robust fusion, it remains unclear at what communication rate most of the achievable tracking gain is obtained, beyond which additional communication resources yield only marginal benefit. We consider stationary agents that observe a moving target through heterogeneous range and bearing measurements, perform local extended Kalman filtering (EKF), quantize their posterior state means, and fuse exchanged information via covariance intersection (CI). Performance is evaluated versus communication rate relative to no-communication baselines, a centralized oracle, and a CI-perfect reference. The results show that communication is not uniformly beneficial: very low rates can degrade performance due to coarse quantization, whereas moderate rates recover most of the achievable gain. In the considered scenario, increasing the rate from 4 to 12 bit/s per agent reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 13.93 m to 6.35 m, while a further increase to 32 bit/s per agent improves it only marginally to 5.93 m. This reveals a clear knee region at moderate rates, beyond which the remaining loss is mainly due to the conservatism of the fusion architecture. Overall, the proposed framework characterizes low-rate degradation, communication-efficient operation, and diminishing returns, while highlighting the joint role of rate and sensing geometry in determining communication benefit.

papers.title: Quantum Hall transformer in a quantum point contact over the full range of transmission
papers.abstract: A recent experiment [Cohen et al., Science 382, 542 (2023)] observed a robustly quantized $e^2/2h$ conductance in a quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall edges (a quantum Hall transformer), which then vanishes at low temperature. While this behavior can be described by a boundary sine gordon (BSG) model derived from electron tunneling, the microscopic motivation for such strong tunneling is unclear. We use an alternative model based on sliding charge density waves and a density inhomogeneity to clarify the BSG description and calculate the conductance over the full range of transmission. Using a perturbative method and a matrix product state calculation, we draw a quantitative connection between the BSG model and the physical quantum Hall system.

papers.title: Coherent control of spinmons
papers.abstract: In this work, we explore a hybrid qubit device where quantum information is encoded by quantum states of a transmon entangled with the spin of a trapped Andreev quasiparticle. We term such devices spinmons. We lift the spinmon Kramers degeneracy by introducing a Zeeman field and develop two routes for full qubit control via electrostatic gates and an AC flux drive, providing multiple directions for experimental implementations. Finally, we compute coherence times, verify the qubit robustness against flux, charge and gate voltage noise sources, and discuss the role of nuclear spin noise.

papers.title: Electrochemical functionalization of graphene rationalized by Hammett and Swain-Lupton parameters
papers.abstract: Graphene's sp^{2}-bonded carbon lattice makes it exceptionally resistant to covalent functionalization, with existing approaches relying on chemically specific and often harsh methods, fragmenting our understanding of its reactivity. Here we show that electric fields of approximately 1 V nm^{-1} in non-aqueous electrolytes enable the electrochemical functionalization of monolayer graphene with a broad range of substituents, leading to two-order-of-magnitude conductance modulation stable over 5,000 cycles and semi-reversible electronic conductor-insulator transitions. Analysis of the oxidation potentials across substituents reveals trends governed by classical descriptors. Species forming localised σ bonds display increasing oxidation potentials with the meta-Hammett constant (σ_m), whereas substituents interacting via delocalised π orbitals follow an inverse dependence on the modified Swain-Lupton resonance parameter (R). These relationships indicate that graphene's oxidation potential increases with the electron-withdrawing strength of the substituent. Our results provide new insights into the electrochemical activity of inert materials under strong electric fields.

papers.title: Non-Bloch Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions with Memory
papers.abstract: Dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) of periodic chains are determined by real Bloch momenta. We identify non-Bloch DQPTs, which occur only in open chains and are determined by complex momenta instead. They arise in a Hermitian chain coupled to a simple substrate, whose memory is treated exactly, and originate from the point-gap winding number $W$ of the projected propagator: for $W\neq0$, open boundaries change both the dynamical free energy and the critical times, even in the thermodynamic limit. We find that both follow from an analytic continuation to complex momenta, and show that $W$ can be measured by particle counting. This reveals a dynamical bulk-boundary correspondence, in which non-Hermitian topology emerges from Hermitian dynamics with memory.

papers.title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
papers.abstract: Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.

papers.title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes
papers.abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for a one-dimensional $p$-$n$ junction diode, conditioned on device length, doping and bias. Using the internal state of the device as predicted by the surrogate we develop a test-suite of quantities of interest including the terminal current, depletion width, peak field and stored charge. The formalism and the quantities are can be extended to asymmetric junction and two-dimensional diodes as shown by means of benchmark analysis. For the one-dimensional symmetric junction surrogate, we obtain 0.11% median $L_1$ error on the electrostatic potential, and 1.5% and 0.61% on the electron and hole densities. Finally, we develop an uncertainty analysis which determines the validity of surrogate answer within the user-specified tolerance.

papers.title: Ghosts in the nanomachine: dynamical slowing-down in the phase-space of nanomechanical strings
papers.abstract: The linear behavior of micro- and nanomechanical devices has been the topic of intense study over the past years. Their nonlinear behavior, on the other hand, continues to provide new and interesting dynamics. This work leverages a cavity opto-mechanical system whose very high sensitivity and low dissipation rate allows to capture the dynamics of fast transients that occur when strongly-driven nonlinear resonators relax to their equilibrium state. We experimentally study the ringdown dynamics of a nanomechanical Duffing resonator in both the time domain and in phase space. The resonator exhibits very different ringdown dynamics depending on whether it is subject to one or two tone driving. In the former case the ringdown follows a regular exponential decay, whereas the latter case shows exotic dynamics such as libration, slowing-down while scattering in phase-space, and ghost slowing-down. We demonstrate that this distinct difference can be attributed to the structure of the phase space itself. Surprisingly, we find that the energy in the resonator changes non-monotonously and that long delay between turning off the drive and the decay of the motion amplitude results in dynamical meta-states.

papers.title: Scattering-force-driven light-sheet fluorescence microscopy for scan-free three-dimensional imaging
papers.abstract: Optical manipulation offers a powerful non-contact approach to precise positioning, directional transport and three-dimensional (3D) imaging of microscale objects. However, positional fluctuations during optical confinement introduce spatial sampling errors that compromise imaging quality and acquisition speed. Here, we demonstrate a scattering-force-driven optical manipulation imaging method that replaces the stepwise scanning of conventional optical trapping with continuous directional transport of microparticles. An axial scattering force generated by a low-numerical-aperture focused beam propels microparticles through a light sheet, while their positions and fluorescence signals are simultaneously recorded to establish direct spatial correspondence between particle motion and tomographic images. Experiments demonstrate that this approach reduces the effects of positional fluctuations on 3D imaging, achieving an axial sampling interval of 0.1 μm and an imaging rate of 250 Hz. The method also enables effective imaging of samples with diverse structural features while reducing optical power requirements by 70%. By combining robust spatial sampling, high-speed acquisition and reduced photodamage, this approach offers a promising route to rapid 3D imaging, dynamic observation and microscale spatial analysis of microparticles and biological specimens.

papers.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
papers.abstract: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

papers.title: Edge intelligence for distributed acoustic sensing with ultracompact neural networks
papers.abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) transforms optical fibres into dense arrays of vibration sensors for continuous, long-range monitoring with high spatial resolution. Yet converting these large-scale measurements into actionable information with compact models that retain task performance remains challenging. Existing artificial-intelligence approaches are typically optimized for specific sensing environments and tasks, but their computational requirements can hinder deployment in compact, power-constrained field systems. Here, we introduce DAS-NanoNet, a framework that automatically constructs lightweight neural networks for different DAS scenarios and tasks, together with OmniDAS, an open benchmark spanning six representative environments. Using lightweight temporal operators tailored to DAS signals, an adaptive neural architecture search strategy derives a compact network for each scenario-task pairing. Across classification, localization, compression, and denoising tasks in diverse DAS applications, DAS-NanoNet consistently yields highly compact architectures. On a six-class dataset, it achieves 99.68% accuracy with only 1,391 trainable parameters, while delivering comparable or better performance with up to 18,098-fold fewer parameters than previously reported high-accuracy networks. Its compact architecture further enables edge deployment, achieving sub 9 $μ$s inference latency on the deployed hardware platform across different DAS applications. DAS-NanoNet provides a route towards edge intelligence for compact, low-power and real-time DAS systems through ultracompact networks tailored to individual sensing scenarios and tasks.

papers.title: Dark-field Search for Quantum Vacuum Signals in the Low-Energy Regime
papers.abstract: We report on the experimental details of a dark-field search for light-by-light scattering signals performed at the High Energy Density (HED) instrument of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) in a pump-probe type experiment colliding the EuXFEL beam with the 300-TW-class near-infrared Relativistic Laser at XFEL (ReLaX) at a center-of-mass photon energy of $ω_\star = 116\,\mathrm{eV}$. Especially in combination with polarization filtering, the dark-field concept allows the signal-to-background ratio to be significantly enhanced and both polarization channels to be recorded. This work elaborates on the experimental setup and the diagnostics used, from the per-shot spatiotemporal-overlap diagnostics, via the polarizing beam splitter, to the characterization of the residual background. Moreover, it provides details on the start-to-end simulations of the setup used for analysis. Accumulating 2751 pump-probe collisions, no excess above background is observed, and an upper limit on the light-by-light scattering cross section of $7\times10^{4}$ times the QED prediction at a 95% confidence level is derived. This is the most stringent bound on low-energy light-by-light scattering achieved to date, representing an improvement by ten orders of magnitude upon previous experimental limits.

papers.title: Integrated Circular Polarisation Beam Shaper Based on Tilted Waveguide Bragg Gratings
papers.abstract: Scalable quantum platforms require optical systems that deliver well-defined polarisation without relying on macroscopic bulk optics or manual alignment, motivating chip-integrated approaches capable of shaping both the spatial mode and the polarisation of the emitted field. By developing a full three-dimensional analytical model of the scattering process together with numerical simulations to design and evaluate the emitted field, we show that tilted waveguide Bragg gratings can act as integrated polarisation beam shapers. We find that scattering two co-propagating, orthogonally polarised pumps on a single grating is fundamentally limited: waveguide birefringence and the difference in scattering efficiency prevent full polarisation control. We overcome this with an orthogonal superimposed-grating architecture in which two gratings driven independently by two pumps propagating perpendicular to each other succeed in generating any desired polarisation output apart from directions in a narrow spatial region. The approach provides a scalable, chip-integrated route to polarisation-engineered light delivery for quantum technologies.

papers.title: Partially temporal coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian and its propagation dynamics
papers.abstract: Optical spatiotemporal vortices carrying transverse photonic orbital angular momentum have become an intense research topic in the recent study of structured light fields. Despite being mainly studied within the framework of fully coherent optical pulses, the complex topologies of the light field are also investigated with partially coherent light sources, offering an alternative pathway in applications. In this work, we theoretically and experimentally investigate partially temporally coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian (STLG) field with independently controllable radial and azimuthal indices. The spatiotemporal topological information, carried by the structured amplified spontaneous emission source, are well preserved in the presence of inherent instantaneous random temporal phase fluctuations. Under combined spatiotemporal astigmatism and group velocity dispersion, the partially temporally coherent STLG field can be converted into spatiotemporal Hermite-Gaussian (STHG) field. Both structures maintain their spatiotemporal characteristics after propagating through scattering media. Partially temporally coherent structured light fields may offer new insights into photonic topology and complex wave dynamics, with potential applications in high-fidelity optical communications and high-dimensional information processing in highly scattering environments.

papers.title: Steering interfacial molecular structures by substrate-molecule charge transfer
papers.abstract: Intermixed self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) provide a powerful approach for tuning inorganic-organic interfaces, but their local structure and energetics often remain elusive. Here, an intermixed stripe phase of fullerene $C_{60}$ and Zn(II)-5,10,15,20-tetrakis(4-aminophenyl)porphyrin (Zn-TAPP) on a Ag(111) surface is identified, establishing a direct link between molecular assembly and charge transfer. Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy (STS) and Kelvin probe force spectroscopy (KPFS) have been used to map electronic states and local contact potential differences (LCPD). Compared to close-packed $C_{60}$ islands, the stripe phase exhibits a larger interfacial dipole and increased occupation of previously unoccupied $C_{60}$ states, consistent with enhanced charge transfer from Ag(111) to $C_{60}$. Analysis indicates that larger $C_{60}$ spacing in the stripe geometry reduces Coulomb repulsion, stabilizing the intermixed phase and enhancing charge transfer with respect to close-packed domains. These results provide direct evidence of charged $C_{60}$ molecules in stripe structures and guidelines for engineering intermixed SAMs with tailored interfacial electronic properties.

papers.title: Light-sheet microscopy in cancer pathology: current applications, clinical challenges and future perspectives
papers.abstract: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) has emerged as a powerful research technology for three-dimensional (3D) visualization of biological tissues and is increasingly applied to human cancer specimens, including optically cleared biopsies and surgical resection samples. In this Perspective article, we review current applications of LSFM in oncology, and discuss how recent developments in microscopy, tissue preparation, labelling, and computational analysis are expanding the possibilities of 3D cancer pathology. Although LSFM has demonstrated the feasibility of large-volume imaging in selected human specimens, its application remains predominantly within research and translational settings and is not currently part of routine clinical pathology. We therefore distinguish demonstrated applications from potential future uses. We discuss how LSFM could eventually contribute to selected diagnostic and surgical workflows by providing 3D information on tumour architecture, spatial heterogeneity, metastatic dissemination, and surgical margins. These applications remain prospective and will require substantial technical, clinical, regulatory, computational, and workflow validation before clinical implementation can be considered. Ultimately, LSFM may complement rather than replace conventional histopathology by extending pathological assessment from two-dimensional tissue sections towards 3D spatial analysis.

papers.title: Wald entropy and Wen-Zee type gauge-curvature coupling in 2+1-dimensional gravity
papers.abstract: The Wen-Zee term is a mixed gauge-curvature coupling in the topological Chern-Simons description of a quantum Hall fluid, encoding the electric charge bound to spatial curvature. We investigate a Lorentz-covariant generalization of this coupling, expanding its scope to black-hole spacetimes and determine its contribution to horizon entropy. Such a coupling arises naturally in three-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity based on the Maxwell algebra. We show that its Wald entropy contribution is a horizon boost charge, given by a loop integral of the additional gauge field projected along the tangent to the bifurcation circle. This contribution can be nonzero even when the mixed term vanishes on shell. We show that the integral admits an Abelian holonomy interpretation when the projection direction is covariantly constant. We evaluate the charge on a flat cosmological solution and, using smooth horizon fields and a specified thermal ensemble, on an AdS-Lorentz black hole. These results connect the geometric response familiar from quantum Hall physics to gravitational horizon thermodynamics.

papers.title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
papers.abstract: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.

papers.title: Non-Markovian quantum-emitter dynamics and bound-state formation in an Aubry--André--Harper photonic lattice
papers.abstract: In non-Markovian light-matter interactions, a spectrally structured bath can alter the evolution of a quantum emitter by modifying the vacuum fluctuations experienced by the emitter. This raises the question of how the localization transition and the associated multifractal critical modes induced by a quasiperiodic potential shape the emitter dynamics. We investigate this scenario in the single-excitation sector for a two-level quantum emitter coupled to an Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) photonic lattice. By externally tuning the strength of the quasiperiodic onsite modulation, the lattice is tuned from the extended to the localized regime through a critical point characterized by multifractal modes. Using modal analysis, we show that the quasiperiodic modulation reshapes the local density of states at the coupling site and thereby controls the effective spectral coupling between the emitter and the lattice. The transient dynamics depend strongly on the spatial and spectral overlap between the emitter and the lattice modes: extended modes below the critical modulation generally produce rapid depopulation, whereas critical and localized modes give rise to coherent back-action and persistent Rabi-like oscillations, with particularly pronounced behavior at the critical point. We further identify emitter-photon bound states whose formation is controlled by the quasiperiodic spectral structure of the bath and whose overlap with the initially excited state leads to partial long-time population trapping. These results establish a direct connection between quasiperiodic localization, non-Markovian dynamics, and emitter-photon bound-state formation.

papers.title: Pulse Laser Deposited GaFeO3 Thin Film Grown on FTO: Correlated Ferroic Orders and Strong Magnetodielectric Coupling at Room Temperature
papers.abstract: Room-temperature single-phase multiferroics exhibiting coupled ferroelectric and magnetic order are promising candidates for next-generation magnetoelectric memory and spintronic technologies. Here, we report the growth of approximately 100.6 nm thick polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films on fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass (FTO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. Core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a reduced Fe2+ concentration and suppressed oxygen-vacancy formation, contributing to reduced leakage current and improved ferroelectric characteristics. The films exhibit robust ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature, confirming the coexistence of ferroic orders within a single phase. Piezoresponse Force Microscopy further demonstrates reversible local polarization switching, accompanied by an asymmetric butterfly loop with coercive voltages of -0.31 V and +1.07 V. The films also exhibit a high relative dielectric constant of approximately 1700 with a relatively low dielectric loss tangent of approximately 2.83 at 1 MHz. Moreover, a significant magnetodielectric coefficient of approximately 2.3% is observed under a relatively small magnetic field of only 0.1 kOe, highlighting strong magnetoelectric coupling. These results establish GaFeO3 thin films as a promising platform for room-temperature multifunctional devices, mainly low-field magnetoelectric memory and spintronic architectures.

papers.title: Symmetry-governed nonlinear metasurface simultaneously enhances circular dichroism, helicity purity, and Q-factor
papers.abstract: Circularly polarized light underpins a broad range of chiroptical and spin-selective photonic technologies, yet extending resonant chirality to nonlinear harmonic emission remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a symmetry-governed mechanism that maps the maximal linear chirality of high-Q degenerate resonances onto the polarization of the generated harmonic. Preserved rotational symmetry protects modal degeneracy and polarization-selection rules, while broken mirror symmetries enable a strong chiroptical response. The metasurface thereby filters the pump polarization and purifies the handedness of the nonlinear output, simultaneously achieving third-harmonic circular dichroism of -0.98, a degree of circular polarization of 0.83, and an effective nonlinear Q-factor of 140. Importantly, the nonlinear emission preserves its handedness even under spatially depolarized excitation, demonstrating robustness to variations in the incident polarization state. These results establish complementary symmetry preservation and breaking as a deterministic route for transferring resonant chirality from linear to nonlinear optical responses, providing a general design principle for nonlinear chiral photonics.

papers.title: Norm of resonance states in quantum scattering and electromagnetic systems
papers.abstract: Resonance states spatially diverge and are thus not square integrable. Instead, their norm is defined by the biorthogonal scalar product of left and right states. We replace the corresponding volume integral over infinite space by a convenient boundary integral in piecewise-homogeneous systems and apply this procedure to diverse physical settings. For a quantum particle in any number of dimensions we treat hard-wall and piecewise-constant potentials. For electromagnetic systems with piecewise-homogeneous material properties, we consider three-dimensional and effectively two-dimensional cavities.

papers.title: Near-Field Engineering of Silica-Shelled Plasmonic Nanoparticles toward Enhanced Near-Infrared Fluorescence
papers.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent molecules often suffer from low quantum yields, limiting their applications in sensing and imaging. Their fluorescence can be enhanced by coupling with plasmonic nanoparticles exhibiting resonances in the same spectral region. However, this approach requires precise nanoscale control over the plasmonic near-field. Here, we combine scanning transmission electron microscopy with electron energy-loss spectroscopy (STEM-EELS) and boundary element electromagnetic simulations to engineer silica-coated anisotropic plasmonic nanoparticles. We synthesised three types of nanoparticles, gold nanorods (AuNRs), gold bipyramids (AuBPs), and silver nanorods (AgNRs) with tunable NIR plasmonic resonances. Silica serves as a dielectric spacer, enabling precise control over the distance between the nanoparticle surface and a potential molecular emitter. To assess their suitability for fluorophore attachment, we investigated the dependence of the electric near-field on silica shell thickness. High-resolution STEM-EELS mapping revealed that thin silica shells (4.4 nm for AuNRs and 3.1 nm for AuBPs) allow most of the near-field to extend beyond the dielectric layer. For AgNRs, a thicker shell of 7.0 nm was required to prevent oxidation while maintaining near-field accessibility. Electromagnetic simulations further evaluated the optimal shell thickness and the dependence of fluorescence enhancement on particle geometry, material, fluorophore internal quantum yield, and fluorophore-metal separation. Together, these results provide practical design guidelines for optimizing particle morphology and sub-10 nm silica shells in plasmonic nanostructures for fluorescence enhancement.

papers.title: Label-free Monitoring of Nucleoid Dynamics of Bacteria for Drug Screening Using Holography
papers.abstract: We introduce holographic microscopy (HM) as a compact, low-cost, label-free, non-specific alternative to fluorescence microscopy (FM) for quantifying bacterial physiological responses during drug screening. Using the regularized inverse holographic volumetric reconstruction (RIHVR) framework, we extract phase maps from HM images and then invert the reconstructed phase to generate fluorescence-like contrast, in which bright inverted-phase regions correspond to bacterial nucleoid content captured by FM signals. We show that this relationship holds across multiple bacterial species, growth stages, drug treatments, and post-treatment time points, demonstrating that HM can consistently capture nucleoid associated structural information without fluorescent labeling. Because HM phase images contain both whole-cell refractive-index information and internal nucleoid-associated contrast, they enable simultaneous quantification of cell boundaries, cell length, nucleoid size, and nucleoid occupancy. These measurements allow drug-induced changes in bacterial morphology and nucleoid organization to be monitored over time. Unlike FM, which can suffer from photobleaching and may perturb live cells through phototoxicity, HM relies on refractive-index variations and maintains stable signal quality for long-term live-cell imaging. By linking label-free phase imaging to nucleoid-scale physiological readouts, this work establishes a path toward automated, high-throughput, and experimentally simpler bacterial drug-screening assays.

papers.title: Focal-Plane Extreme Adaptive Optics for Deep Super Resolution Imaging and Nanolithography
papers.abstract: Super resolution optical imaging and nanolithography enable nanoscale observation and fabrication, but high order, spatially varying phase and amplitude aberrations in optically heterogeneous media severely limit their performance at depth. Here we introduce focal-plane extreme adaptive optics (FP-ExAO), which moves beyond conventional phase conjugate correction by directly sensing and controlling the focal-plane complex field. This terminal field captures aberrations accumulated throughout the optical system. A state space formulation directly links deformable mirror commands to the focal field, avoiding explicit plane by plane Fourier optics modelling, while information theoretically optimal probing and closed-form control enable rapid field estimation and correction. Cascaded deformable mirrors further enable FP-ExAO to correct coupled phase-amplitude and spatially varying aberrations. In three-dimensional (3D) single molecule localization microscopy (SMLM), FP-ExAO enables imaging to 160 um depth in brain tissue and beyond 60 um in kidney tissue, while maintaining approximately 18 nm localization precision across a 75 um x 75 um corrected field, with a 16-fold larger field of view and more than tenfold faster correction than conventional AO methods. These capabilities meet the imaging requirements for 3D deep tissue optical connectome reconstruction and quantitative super resolution pathology. In stimulated emission depletion (STED) nanolithography, FP-ExAO reduces the minimum written linewidth from 251.1 nm without correction to 88.8 nm at a depth of 160 um in photoresist. FP-ExAO establishes a new adaptive optics paradigm for deep nanoscale optical readout and writing.

papers.title: Th$^{4+}$ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$
papers.abstract: The low-energy nuclear isomeric transition of $^{229}$Th is a promising frequency reference for a solid-state nuclear optical clock. Wide-band-gap fluoride crystals such as CaF$_2$ offer transparent hosts for embedding Th nuclei at high density. Substitution of Th$^{4+}$ for Ca$^{2+}$ requires charge compensation, linking the local defect structure to nuclear quadrupole splitting. We use first-principles calculations to examine neutral Th dimers compensated by four interstitial F ions ($\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$). Screening different compensation geometries by their relative formation energies identifies a family of low-energy configurations with closely similar local structures. These configurations share large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimental high-EFG site 3. Their calculated quadrupole splittings are further compared with the measured C13 spectra. Together, the energetic and spectroscopic results support $\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$-compensated Th dimers as candidate microscopic structures for site 3 in Th:CaF$_2$.

papers.title: Spatial-Mode Selection for Local Mineral Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Absorption-band depth measures the fractional decrease in mineral reflectance below its local continuum. Recovering this feature strength for a small mineral region supports quantitative comparisons between regions, but diffraction mixes its light with the surroundings. Conventional spectral fitting can separate mean contributions; it cannot remove background photon noise already recorded. We develop a quantum-inspired measurement framework that uses spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) to retain the target absorption response while reducing background acceptance before detection. The framework connects finite mineral-region geometry and reference spectra to estimation precision. A loss-dependent design condition identifies when adding SPADE exposure improves on direct imaging (DI) under fixed-response Poisson measurements with unknown scene parameters. Joint inference from initial DI observations and both mode ports estimates target depth together with an unknown, spatially shared background spectrum. In equal-time simulations that include localization uncertainty, alignment time, calibration, and detector costs, this acquisition reduces depth root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 14\%--26\% across five absorption strengths relative to all-pixel DI with the same background freedom. These results use a supplied target feature shape and geometry, with target continuum slope fitted and curvature fixed. The analysis separates optical selectivity from parameter ambiguity and acquisition cost, providing a quantitative basis for spatial-mode receiver design in local mineral spectroscopy.

papers.title: Optical vortex generation by magnons with spin-orbit-coupled light
papers.abstract: Light possesses both spin and orbital angular momentum. In spatially asymmetric optical fields, these properties undergo spontaneous coupling, referred to as optical spin-orbit coupling. The study of the coupling has recently become central in modern optics due to its substantial applications in communications, sensing, and quantum control. A key challenge is to clarify the relationship between the origins of spatially asymmetric optical fields and the resulting spin-orbit coupling. Current research focuses on materials and configurations exhibiting spatial asymmetry, such as focusing lenses, interfaces, inhomogeneous media, and metasurfaces. However, Maxwell's equations indicate that matter can introduce both spatial and temporal asymmetry into optical fields. For instance, magnetic ordering breaks the time-reversal symmetry of interacting optical fields via the magneto-optic effect, introducing nonreciprocity in the resulting optical phenomena. Despite the importance, optical phenomena involving both spatially and temporally asymmetric optical fields remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that breaking time and spatial symmetries through magnons and light focusing, respectively, transforms an input Gaussian beam into a specific optical vortex beam in a nonreciprocal manner. This phenomenon is quantitatively explained by integrating the physics of magnon-induced Brillouin light scattering with optical spin-orbit coupling. The observed conservation of total angular momentum, encompassing both magnons and photons, further indicates that magnons can control both spin and orbital angular momentum of light. Finally, we outline future research directions enabled by asymmetric optical fields in both space and time.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal coupling enables tunable exceptional-point response in non-Hermitian circuits
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit characteristic square-root spectral responses to weak perturbations, with response magnitudes governed by configuration-dependent prefactors that are often relatively small. Modulating these prefactor while preserving the exceptional characteristics offers an additional degrees of freedom for engineering non-Hermitian sensing responses. Here, we report a nonreciprocal non-Hermitian circuit system with gyrator-meditated coupling that supports a continuous family of EP configurations. Unlike reciprocal coupling, which typically yields a unique EP configuration for balanced gain and loss, nonreciprocal coupling allows the directional forward and backward coupling strengths to be varied while maintaining their product and thus preserving the EP condition and yielding a library of EPs. This additional freedom enables continuous control of the frequency-splitting magnitude without modifying the square-root characteristic dependence on absolute perturbation strength. We show that the spectral splitting induced by a given absolute resistance perturbation can be enhanced by appropriately adjusting the coupling asymmetry. Theoretical predictions, circuit simulations, and experimental reflection-spectrum measurements consistently confirms this tunable response. Our results establish nonreciprocal coupling as an alternative approach for engineering and enhancing EP-induced perturbative responses without changing their characteristic branch-point scaling.

papers.title: Signatures of Narrowband and Ultrashort-Pulse-Like Probing in Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering Using Twin Beams and Sum-Frequency Generation Readout
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) driven by bright twin beams with sum-frequency generation (SFG) readout. Expressing the SFG output in terms of quantum-field correlation functions yields multiple correlation structures with distinct properties associated with different interaction pathways on the bra and ket sides. Among them, frequency correlations between the CARS probe and SFG gating fields enable the two fields to act collectively as an effective narrowband probe, avoiding probe-induced spectral convolution. When this behavior appears on either the bra or ket side, the other retains Raman relaxation information as if probed by an ultrashort pulse.

papers.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
papers.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. Under high-energy excitation, the patterns appear up to ~3.5$\times$ brighter and demonstrate emission enhancement trends consistent with well-established nanophotonic scaling laws. We also report a novel functionality we call "remote outcoupling," in which the nanophotonic patterns emit light that is generated in another region of the scintillator, without being directly excited themselves. Our monolithic nanofabrication approach extends nanophotonic scintillators into the bulk, which is an important step towards total control over scintillation using photonic design.

papers.title: Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
papers.abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies based on van der Waals materials.

papers.title: Direct laser-written optomechanical double membranes in an optical microcavity
papers.abstract: Optomechanical membrane-in-the-middle systems that comprise several coupled compliant membranes offer enhanced optomechanical coupling and collective dynamics. Recent realizations were fundamentally restricted to two membranes and to limited structural optimization of the involved membranes due to their intricate fabrication and experimental integration. Here, we present a fiber-based Fabry-Perot microcavity incorporating monolithically integrated double-membrane resonators fabricated by 3D direct laser writing. We realize controllable mechanical mode hybridization of membranes with coupling rates of up to $J_{\mathrm{mech}}/2π= 0.16$ MHz, exceeding the mechanical linewidths. We demonstrate enhanced collective optomechanical coupling of the membrane stack's breathing mode, reaching collective coupling strengths of up to $g_{\mathrm{col}}^{(-)}/2π\approx 0.1$ MHz. Our transfer-matrix calculations predict further substantial enhancements with realistic reductions of membrane thickness and spacing, and a larger number of membranes. Our results establish direct laser-written membrane arrays as a scalable platform for multimode cavity optomechanics, combining tunable mechanical interactions, enhanced collective optomechanical coupling, and scalability towards larger mechanically coupled resonator systems.

papers.title: Photon-starved imaging through turbulence at the diffraction limit
papers.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence limits the resolution of ground-based imaging through rapidly evolving wavefront distortions. Fast acquisition can effectively freeze turbulence, but the restricted photon budget makes joint scene and wavefront recovery challenging. Here, we introduce Turbulence-Aware Poisson Blind Deconvolution (TAP-BD), which uses optical phase diversity to provide complementary measurements within a short acquisition window and increase wavefront information per detected photon. Poisson denoising and physics-informed optimization translate this information gain into joint recovery of the scene and a shared turbulence wavefront, with phase estimation errors approaching the Cramer--Rao lower bound in simulations. Experiments demonstrate reliable recovery from only a few tens of measurements under strong turbulence, with additional validation under severe photon scarcity. Simulations further show robustness to scintillation and temporal evolution over short acquisition windows. These results support photon-efficient imaging through turbulence, with potential applications in astronomy, remote sensing, and space situational awareness, particularly for time-sensitive observations.

papers.title: Ultrafast All-Optical Polarization Control in a Plasmonic Metasurface by Selective Hot-Electron Heating of Orthogonal Gold Nanorods
papers.abstract: Metamaterials tailor light's degrees of freedom through static designs, but sub-picosecond, all-optical control without sacrificing signal throughput remains challenging. Here, a metasurface is presented whose unit cell contains two independent, orthogonal and spectrally detuned Au nanorod resonators. A femtosecond pump polarized along either nanorod selectively heats its electrons, modulating one polarization channel while the other serves as an essentially unperturbed phase reference, turning a static wave retarder into an ultrafast, all-optically reconfigurable one. The transient response is computed by coupling a Three-Temperature Model, benchmarked against published experiments, with Finite-Difference Time-Domain simulations. Hot electrons damp and red-shift the pumped resonance, modulating the amplitude ratio and phase retardation of the two channels. In transmission at normal incidence and sub-mJ cm$^{-2}$ fluence, a 45$^\circ$ probe undergoes changes of $\approx$10$^\circ$ in ellipticity and $\approx$15$^\circ$ in optical rotation within $\approx$100 fs (relaxation time $\approx$4 ps), while its transmittance ($\approx$0.4) changes by at most $\approx$0.05. A second, delayed pump along the other nanorod raises these changes to $\approx$15$^\circ$ and $\approx$22$^\circ$ and, for a suitably polarized probe, cancels the intensity change of the first within $\approx$60 fs while the polarization stays changed. Selective all-optical control of independent resonators offers a practical route to transmissive ultrafast polarization control.

papers.title: Broadband characterization of polarization mode dispersion for quantum communication channels
papers.abstract: We present a method for characterizing depolarization in fiber channels carrying broadband polarization-encoded optical signals. Wavelength-dependent polarization mode dispersion maps each input polarization to a trajectory on the Poincaré sphere; we show that the singular value decomposition of the band-averaged rotation matrix yields, in closed form, the optimal input states, the associated mutually unbiased measurement bases, and the resulting projection error probabilities. The three singular values provide a compact, bandwidth-dependent channel signature that distinguishes first- from higher-order dispersion, and yield the bandwidth at which the worst-case error probability reaches 3% as a practical filtering budget. We perform a second-order analysis of the band average that treats the two higher-order mechanisms: variation of the differential group delay at a fixed principal-state axis and wander of that axis with wavelength. We characterize 12 deployed fiber links in Masdar City and demonstrate mitigation by concatenating two channels through a single polarization controller, a step towards nonlocal compensation. The analysis is implemented in an openly available Python library for fiber-channel characterization.

papers.title: Stability Study of Photo-inscribed Bragg Gratings in Sapphire Fibers at Very High Temperature
papers.abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser in sapphire fibers were subjected to thermal cycling up to 1500$\degree$C. Adding a multimode silica fiber reduces modal interference, improves the quality of the Bragg spectrum and the measurement accuracy. The measurement uncertainty is about 1.9$\degree$C at 1500$\degree$C.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal Floquet tunneling dynamics of spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a non-Hermitian double-well potential
papers.abstract: The stable tunneling dynamics in non-Hermitian quantum systems is one of the fundamental issues in the study of quantum transport. Nonreciprocal coupling, as another crucial manifestation of non-Hermiticity, exerts significant regulatory effects on the stability of quantum devices and on spin tunneling dynamics. Here we place spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a double-well potential with gain and loss, and investigate the effect of nonreciprocal coupling on the system dynamics. Through an analytical analysis of the Floquet states and the quasi-energy spectrum under periodic driving, we obtain the PT-symmetry phase diagram of the system. We further explore the synergistic regulation mechanism of several factors---including the strength of nonreciprocal coupling, the non-Hermitian strength arising from gain-loss, and the periodic driving---on stable spin-flip tunneling. The results show that precise manipulation of nonreciprocity and gain-loss can substantially enlarge the stable parameter region. In nonreciprocal systems with balanced gain and loss, the continuity or discreteness of the stable parameter region is determined by the parity of the driving-frequency ratio $Ω/ω$, and the spin-flip tunneling can be precisely controlled through the parameters $λ$ and $2\varepsilon/ω$. For the unbalanced gain-loss scenario, the equilibrium conditions for achieving stable spin-flip tunneling under different parities of $Ω/ω$ are further provided. These findings offer a new theoretical approach for realizing robust spin-flip tunneling, provide guiding significance for the study of quantum-state transport in non-Hermitian ultracold atomic systems, and also serve as a reference for the experimental design of novel spin-based quantum devices.

papers.title: Engineering Canalized Near-Field Radiative Heat Transfer between Fixed Nanoparticles with Twisted $α$-MoO$_3$ Trilayers
papers.abstract: Canalized phonon polaritons in twisted van der Waals crystals offer a route to control nanoscale thermal energy flow. Building on the established twisted $α$-MoO$_3$ trilayer platform, we examine how internal twist angles modify near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) between a prescribed nanoparticle pair while both the nanoparticle axis and the bottom-layer crystallographic orientation remain fixed. Under this constraint and at equal total $α$-MoO$_3$ thickness, the optimized trilayer reaches 2.84 times the bilayer maximum radiative power, while its mean power over the sampled internal twist configurations is 1.51 times the bilayer value. The second internal twist coordinate also enlarges the set of configurations supporting strong transfer, with local angular tolerance when either internal angle is varied separately. Momentum-space Green-tensor diagnostics and real-space energy-density maps associate the enhancement with stronger receiver-directed scattering and improved channel alignment. Selected trilayer configurations retain enhanced coupling across the sampled family of nanoparticle resonances and at long distances. These results quantify the additional internal configurational freedom available for engineering radiative heat transfer under a fixed laboratory-frame geometry.

papers.title: Extending the limits of rotationally resolved mid-IR spectroscopy: an accurate model of trioxane derived from combining Fourier transform and sub-Doppler measurements
papers.abstract: 1,3,5-Trioxane, a polyoxymethylene (POM) molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry and astrophysics, exhibits a dense rovibrational spectrum that challenges high-resolution spectroscopic characterization. Here, we report an extensive study of its $ν$ 5 CO symmetric stretching mode (960-1000 cm -1 ) by combining broadband high-resolution FTIR spectroscopy (0.001 cm -1 resolution, >2000 transitions) with SI-traceable sub-Doppler saturated absorption measurements using frequency-stabilized CO 2 lasers and a frequency-comb-referenced quantum cascade laser. The latter achieve lineposition uncertainties as low as 40 kHz, revealing inaccuracies in the FTIR frequency scale. A frequency-scale correction is determined by maximizing the global consistency of the complete spectroscopic data set. A global least-squares Hamiltonian fit combining the calibrated FTIR data, the SI-traceable sub-Doppler measurements and previously reported millimeter-wave rotational transitions yields a refined spectroscopic model. The resulting analysis significantly improves the precision of the rotational, quartic, and sextic constants for both the ground and $ν$ 5 excited vibrational states. This work extends mid-infrared frequency metrology to the largest molecule studied to date (12 atoms), providing a dense set of reference transitions for frequency calibration around 970 cm -1 . The resulting spectroscopic parameters reach relative uncertainties as low as 3.7 x 10 -10 for the band origin, making them valuable for molecular databases used in astrophysics and atmospheric physics, as well as for precision measurements in fundamental physics. Additionally, the observed line shapes indicate the absence of significant intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) within the investigated energy range, while a few discrepancies in the Hamiltonian fit suggest the onset of weak perturbations, demonstrating the sensitivity of the present approach to probe subtle intramolecular couplings in complex polyatomic spectra. papers.title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.

papers.title: Confocal ellipsoidal displaced Gregorian structure for stand-off millimeter-wave imaging
papers.abstract: Reflective-based structures are favorable candidates as the optical section of millimeter-wave and terahertz (THz) stand-off imaging systems due to decreasing frequency-dependent losses and aberrations compared to refractive-based counterparts. In this paper, we propose a simple confocal ellipsoidal displaced Gregorian (CEDG) dual-mirror configuration for stand-off imaging systems that exhibits superior performance in terms of mitigating optical blockage and enabling object scanning. The proposed structure is composed of a standard elliptical main mirror, which focuses the emanated rays on the focal plane, and a modified secondary mirror (SM) that reduces the optical blockage effect and improves the imaging performance of the structure. A detailed step-by-step procedure is proposed for constructing the structure, followed by an analytical study and deriving closed-form design equations. By performing ray tracing simulations, it is observed that the optical blockage of the proposed CEDG structure is reduced compared with the standard Gregorian. Also, the resolution and the depth-of-focus (DoF) are obtained at 1.5 cm and 49.7 cm in full-wave simulations, respectively, demonstrating good agreement with the theoretical predictions. Moreover, the scanning performance of the CEDG structure is investigated by utilizing the tilting of the SM and feed point displacement, presenting a maximum field-of-view (FoV) of 40 cm at a distance of 3 m, which is acceptable for modern practical stand-off imaging systems. Finally, the capability of the proposed structure for tuning the stand-off distance by lateral displacement of the feeding source is verified. As a result, the proposed compact, low-cost configuration shows potential for practical mm-wave and THz stand-off imaging systems.

papers.title: Drift-induced nonreciprocity in image-polariton-mediated dipole emission
papers.abstract: Electrical current bias offers a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal light propagation at the nanoscale. Here, we theoretically explore drift-induced nonreciprocity in graphene heterostructures containing hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), where graphene plasmons interact with hBN phonon polaritons in the infrared. Both the random-phase approximation and the Boltzmann transport equation are used to characterize the nonlocal optical response of drift-biased graphene. We compare graphene on hBN with an image-polaritonic structure comprising graphene, a thin hBN spacer, and a gold substrate. Carrier drift produces pronounced directional shifts of the polariton dispersion, while coupling to hBN phonon polaritons strongly modifies the nonreciprocal response. In the image-polaritonic structure, the graphene polaritons become up to twice as confined while retaining a comparable Fizeau shift. The nonreciprocal polariton dispersion produces directional near-field emission and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions, the latter quantified through the cross density of optical states, reaching a left-right dissymmetry of up to ~40%. Our results identify image polaritons in drift-biased graphene as a compact, electrically tunable platform for directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.
